header.running_head: Speaking the Truth to the Ameer and Rejecting his Command if it Conflicts with the Commands of Allaah

The Narration of Hadhrat Hasan (RA) in this Regard

Hadhrat Hasan reports that when Ziyaad dispatched Hadhrat Hakam bin Amr Ghifaari (RA) as governor of Khurasan, the Muslims there managed to win a large amount of booty. Ziyaad then wrote to Hadhrat Hakam (RA) saying, "The Ameerul Mu'mineen (Hadhrat Mu'aawiya (RA)) has written to say that all the gold and silver should be reserved for him and should therefore not be distributed amongst the Muslims." Hadhrat Hakam (RA) wrote back to Ziyaad saying, "You have written to me about the letter of the Ameerul Mu'mineen. However, I have received the Book of Allaah before the letter of the Ameerul Mu'mineen (I shall therefore not obey his command which contradicts that of the Qur'aan). I swear by Allaah that even if the skies and earth have to close up on a person, Allaah will create an escape for him between them and give him peace if he is one who fears Allaah."
Hadhrat Hakam (RA) then had an announcer announce to the people that they should present themselves for the booty by the morning. He then distributed the booty (including the gold and silver) amongst the people. When he did this, Hadhrat Mu'aawiya (RA) sent some people to arrest Hadhrat Hakam (RA) and place him in shackles. Hadhrat Hakam (RA) passed away in these shackles and was buried in Khurasan. He said, "I shall contest (my case against Mu'aawiya (RA) in the court of Allaah)." [^2]

Another narration adds that after Hadhrat Hakam (RA) had distributed the booty amongst the people, he prayed, "O Allaah! If You have any good for me with You, then raise me to You." He then passed away in the town of Maroo in Khurasan. [^3] Isaaba (Vol.1 Pg.347) states that it was actually when Hadhrat Hakam (RA) received the letter of Ziyaad noting his displeasure, he prayed to Allaah (for a swift death), after which he passed away.
The Way that Hadhrat Imraan bin Husayn (RA) Dealt with the Zakaah Monies

Hadhrat Ataa reports that Ziyaad or his son once sent Hadhrat Imraan bin Husayn (RA) to collect Zakaah. When Hadhrat Imraan (RA) returned, he brought nothing back. "Where is the money?" asked Ziyaad (or his son). "Did you send me to bring back any money?" Hadhrat Imraan (RA) asked, "I collected it as we used to do during the time of Rasulullaah ﷺ and used it in the avenues we used it during the time of Rasulullaah ﷺ (I distributed it amongst the needy of the area)." [^4]
Ibn Abi Aasim, Baghawi, Ahmad, Bukhari in his Taareekh, Baawardi and Tabraani, as quoted in Isaaba (Vol.1 Pg.403). Haythami (Vol.5 Pg.234) has commented on the chain of narrators.
Haakim (Vol.3 Pg.471), narrating from reliable sources, as confirmed by Dhahabi.
